gitCommit.subject: fix(qa): keep the agents out of node_modules and .git, and document security (#3)
gitCommit.body:
fix(qa): keep the agents out of node_modules and .git, and document security (#3)

* docs: explain why the kit exists and how each step reduces risk

Lead with the problem a code review leaves open, then explain which
risk each step of the workflow answers, when to use it, and what has
to be maintained.

* feat(qa): add a bounded repair loop

When the verification fails, qa/repair-loop.sh sends the short failure
summary to a repair agent that may change the application but not the
tests, their configuration, the dependencies or the kit. After each
repair it checks that the approved tests are unchanged, then verifies
again, up to three verifications.

- qa-repairer agent with its own settings and a "repair" guard mode
- tests for the loop's decisions and for the repair guard
- remove the Write(...) and Glob(...) permission rules, which never match

* feat(qa): add an advisory AI review of the smoke screenshots

A pixel comparison says a page changed, not that it is broken. The smoke
test now keeps a desktop and a phone screenshot, and CI asks a vision
model to look for overflowing text, overlapping elements, empty sections
and controls off screen. Findings become pull request warnings; the step
never fails the build and is skipped without an API key.

- qa/visual-review.ts with a structured output schema, and its tests
- the official API SDK, pinned to a release at least two weeks old

* feat(ci): run the QA agents in GitHub Actions

Two workflows:
- "QA write tests", started by hand with a ticket key, runs the QA writer
  and opens a pull request into feat/<ticket> with the RED tests.
  Approving it, with a reason per criterion, is the human review.
- "QA verify", on pull requests into main, checks that a collaborator
  approved the latest version of the tests and that they are unchanged,
  then runs the QA verifier and the full suite. As a required check, it
  blocks the merge.

The review package (criteria, RED reports, review request) is committed
in qa-reviews/<ticket>/, so that CI can check the approval. The kit runs
on an application in another folder (QA_PROJECT_DIR). The agent's
commands get no credentials, and the full suite runs in a step without
the API key. The demo gains TICKET-43, a "Clear search" button.

* fix(qa): keep the agents out of node_modules and .git

The guard now refuses any agent write in node_modules/ or .git/. A repair
agent could otherwise patch Vitest or Playwright so that a broken
application passes, or add a git hook that runs on the next commit.

The repair loop also records node_modules/ and the git config, hooks and
info files before the first verification, keeps that record in memory,
and compares it after every repair and every verification. A change stops
the loop with code 3, even when it comes from code that the tests ran.

The repair settings no longer deny reports/: Claude Code applies these
deny rules to sandboxed commands too, which kept the test tools from
writing their reports. The guard still blocks the agent's own edits there.

* docs: gather the security model, gaps and limits in the README
